summary: The root LDD primarily signifies intense contention, dispute, or obstinacy. It describes someone who is vehemently argumentative, quarrelsome, or stubbornly persistent in their opposition.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: لَدّ, originally لَدِدَ, (second pers. لَدِدْتَ, L,) aor. لَدَدَ, (L, Msb,) inf. n. لَدَدٌ (S, A, L, Msb,) He was violent, or vehement, in contention, or altercation; in dispute; in litigation. (S, A, L, Msb.) لَدَّهُ, (S, L, Msb, K,) aor. لَدَدَ, (S, L, Msb,) inf. n. لَدٌّ, (L, Msb,) He overcame him in contention, or altercation; in dispute; in litigation: (S, * L, K: *) or he opposed him violently, or vehemently, in contention, or altercation; in dispute; in litigation.
لدّد بِهِ i. q. ندّد به, (L, K,) i. e., He rendered him notorious, or infamous. (L.)

لادّهُ, inf. n. لِدَادٌ (A, Msb) and مُلَادَّةٌ, (A,) He contended with him violently, or vehemently, in an altercation; in a dispute; in a litigation. (A, Msb.) مَا زِلْتُ أُلَادُّ عَنْكَ I ceased not to repel from thee; or, to defend thee. (S.)

الدّهُ He found him to be such as is called أَلَدّ [ violent, or vehement, in contention, &c ]. (TA.) الدّ بِهِ He opposed him in contention, or altercation; in dispute; in litigation. (TA.) See also 1 and 3.

تلدّد (tropical:) He turned his face to the right and left, (S, L, K,) in confusion, perplexity, or amazement: (L, K:) from اللَّدِيدَانِ signifying “ the two sides ” of the neck. (S, L.) He tarried, or waited, in expectation. (K, TA.)
التدّ, (S, L, K,) and التدّ لَدُودًا, (S, L,) He swallowed a medicine, or draught, of the kind termed لَدُود. (S, * L, * K.) See also لُدّض. التدّ عَنْهُ He declined from him, or it. (K.)
لَدٌّ: see لَادٌّ. A [ sack of the kind called ] جُوَالِق: (S, L, K:) like لَبِيدٌ. (TA.)

لَدُودٌ: see لَادٌّ. لَدُودٌ and A medicine (or draught, As, L) that is poured into one of the two sides of the mouth (As, S, L, K) by means of the instrument called مُسْعُط: (L, K:) pl. أَلِدَّةٌ: (S, L, K:) from اللَّدِيدَانِ signifying “ the two sides ” of a valley. (S, L.) It is said in a proverb, جَرَى مِنْهُ مَجْرَى اللَّدُودِ [ It acted upon him, or affected him, like the medicine, or draught, termed لَدُود; i. e., unpleasantly, or disagreeably]. (ISk, S.) See Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 282

لَدِيدٌ: see لَدُودٌ. لَدِيدَانِ The two sides of a valley: (S, A, L:) each of them is called لَدِيدٌ: (L:) and the two sides of the neck, (S, A, L, K,) below the ears: (L, K:) or the two lateral muscles of the neck: (M, L:) the two sides of the mouth: (A, L:) and of the penis: (L:) and (as some say, L) of anything: (L, K:) pl. أَلِدَّةٌ: (S, L, K:) and لَدِيدٌ, accord. to AA, signifies the outside of the neck. (L.) See لَادٌّ.

لَادٌّ and, (S, L, Msb, K,) the latter having an intensive sense, and, which is an inf. n. used as an epithet [and therefore also intensive], (Msb,) A man who overcomes in contention, or altercation; in dispute; in litigation: (S, * L, K: *) or, who opposes violently, or vehemently, and very violently, or vehemently, in contention, or altercation; in dispute; in litigation: (Msb:) and (S, L, Msb, K) and and (S, L, K) a man violent, or vehement, in contention, or altercation; in dispute; in…
أَلَدُّ and أَلَنْدَدٌ and يَلَنْدَدٌ and أُلَيْدُّ: see لَادٌّ.
مَلْدُودٌ A man who has had a medicine, or draught, of the kind termed لَدُود administered to him. (S, L, K.)
مَا لِى عَنْهُ مُلْتَدٌّ I have no way of avoiding, or escaping, it: (S, L, K:) as also مُحْتَدٌّ. (S, L.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
